Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for New Zealand's reply. Australia are seen in a huddle near the ropes before they disperse to take their places on the field. They are joined by the two Kiwi openers. In the absence of Devon Conway, it will be Will Young to open the innings alongside Tom Latham. Mitchell Starc will start with the new ball for the Aussies. Here we go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

It has been an extremely frustrating morning for New Zealand. At the start of the day, they were hopeful of restricting Australia to 300. However, it did not go according to plan for them, as Cameron Green and Josh Hazlewood kept the Kiwi pacers at bay. The hosts did not help their cause and were all over the place with their lines and lengths, allowing the Aussie batters to have it their way. The heads began to drop for New Zealand as Tim Southee was left scratching his head to find the last wicket. Due to their in-out fields, Green was able to manoeuvre the strike and frustrated the Kiwis even more. Moreover, the Kiwi bowlers gave away as many as 41 extras which sums up the inconsistencies in their lines and lengths. Matt Henry was the standout for New Zealand, ending with a five-wicket haul. The hosts will have to put this first session behind them and start afresh post-lunch. The Kiwi openers will face a stern test first up with the new ball and it will be interesting to see how they fare against the Aussie pace trio. Join us back in a short while to see how it all pans out in the second session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 104 runs, 30.1 overs and 1 wicket. Australia have finally been bowled out for 383 but the first session here on Day 2 has well and truly belonged to them. Having begun the day with an overnight score of 279, Cameron Green and Josh Hazlewood got together and piled the misery on the hosts. Green picked up where he left off on the opening day and continued to tick along nicely. Hazlewood gave a good account of his batting potential and was prepared to hang in there. Green used his smarts well to shield Hazlewood and soon got to his 150. The two Aussie batters were even helped by the lack of intensity shown in the field by New Zealand. Even after getting to the landmark, Green put his head down and stretched the total alongside Hazlewood. The duo put on 116 runs for the 10th wicket, the highest last-wicket stand in Tests by any team against New Zealand, to propel their side's total over 380. Hazlewood's long vigil eventually came to an end as Green remained unbeaten on 174.

OUT! TAKEN! Matt Henry breaks through for New Zealand. He gets his fifth wicket and Australia have been bowled out for 383. Henry comes in from over the wicket and goes full, around off, Josh Hazlewood gets lured into the drive as he looks to hit this one on the up. He stays leg side of the ball and reaches out to play the shot. Ends up chipping it straight down the throat of Rachin Ravindra at mid off where he reverse cups it in front of his face. That will also be LUNCH on Day 2!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin! The two umpires make their way into the middle followed by the fielders of New Zealand. The centurion Cameron Green alongside Josh Hazlewood will resume their stay at the crease for Australia. Matt Henry has the ball in hand and will start the proceedings for the Kiwis. Let's play says the umpire and here we go..

Australia, on the other hand, started well with their openers laying a solid foundation. Mitchell Marsh's counterattack, supported by Cameron Green's resilience, led a spirited fightback after a flurry of wickets fell quickly. Green's exceptional performance, culminating in another Test century, has bolstered Australia's position. They will now be aiming to surpass the 300-run mark and capitalize on favourable bowling conditions with the seamers likely to benefit from overhead conditions and assistance from the pitch. As we look ahead to Day 2, who do you think will seize the advantage in this enthralling contest? Stay tuned as the action comes to you in a bit.

The momentum on Day 1 swung back and forth, with the hosts seizing control of the game during the second session by dismissing half of the Aussie side after they had made a solid start. However, the bowlers seemed to lose their rhythm in the final session, allowing Cameron Green to dominate and put them under some pressure. Despite this, Matt Henry stood out for his fiery spells throughout the day, claiming 4 crucial wickets and keeping the Kiwis' hopes alive. The Kiwis will now be eager to wrap up the Australian innings as soon as possible.

Right then, as the first day's play draws to a close, Australia will be the happier of the two sides. With the surface already playing tricks, New Zealand would want to get that last wicket quickly on Day 2 and get into bat. The Kiwis will be required to bat well in the first innings, given that they have to bat last on this uneven surface. As far as Australia are concerned, the onus will be on Cameron Green to bat for as long as possible to stretch the first-inning total close to 300. Day 2 will begin at 3.30 am IST (10 pm GMT, the previous day), but you can join us earlier for the build-up. Until then, take care and goodbye!

The man of the moment, Cameron Green is down for a quick chat. He says the century feels good and is happy with how his team is set up on this difficult pitch. Adds that after the 20th over the ball kept coming back sharply in and was difficult to bat. States that he and Mitchell Marsh played well and Marsh took the pressure off him. Mentions that the overhead conditions will be crucial for Day 2 and says the match is poised well. Concludes that the Kiwis have a pretty strong lineup and they will have to bowl really well.

As for New Zealand, they will be disappointed that they were not able to bowl Australia out, having had them in a spot of bother at 176-6. New Zealand, having won the toss, sought early breakthroughs but settled for containing Australia's scoring. Led by Tim Southee's decision to bowl first, the Kiwi pacers, particularly Matt Henry, troubled the Australian openers with disciplined bowling. His persistence paid off with the crucial wicket of Steven Smith just before Lunch, providing New Zealand a positive takeaway from the session. After a not-so-great first session, the hosts needed early wickets to start the afternoon session on the right foot. The Kiwi pacers bowled with much more discipline than they did in the first session and went full as well to be rewarded with three wickets in the second session. New Zealand continued making inroads in the third session but they faced stiff resistance from Green and just could not see the back of him. Matt Henry was the pick of the bowlers for the hosts on the opening day with four wickets to his name,

SESSION SUMMARY - 132 runs, 32 overs and 5 wickets. It's advantage Australia and thanks to Cameron Green's special ton, the visitors have taken the honours on the opening day of the first Test. On a surface where run-scoring has been difficult, Green looked the part and seemed to be batting on a different surface to everyone else. Australia, inserted into bat under overcast conditions, relied on Steven Smith and Usman Khawaja to navigate the challenging first hour. Both batters demonstrated resilience, with Smith punishing loose deliveries and Khawaja gaining confidence after a shaky start. Despite losing Smith before Lunch, Australia established a solid foundation, with Khawaja and Marnus Labuschagne partnering to prevent further setbacks. It was a far-from-ideal start for Australia in the second session. The visitors were dealt an early blow in the form of the tentative-looking Marnus Labsuchange before losing Khawaja and Travis Head in quick succession. Mitchell Marsh then took the attack to the opposition with Cameron Green to wrestle the initiative back in his side's favour. However, he failed to kick on, and Alex Carey could not do much either, which put the Aussies on the back foot. Green carried on his merry way and forged stands with the tail to keep the scoreboard ticking. With nine wickets down, Green was left with no option but to go for big shots to get to his second Test ton and he brought it up in fine fashion in the last over of the day.

Australia, despite a promising start in the first session, have seen their fortunes take a downward turn in this session. Marnus Labuschagne, who struggled to find his rhythm, continued his streak of low scores being dismissed for just 1 run off 27 deliveries shortly after Lunch. Despite Usman Khawaja's determined efforts and his hard-earned innings, he was unable to fend off a particularly impressive delivery and fell after a gritty start, adding to Australia's woes. Travis Head, too, couldn't contribute substantially to the scoreboard and was swiftly dismissed, compounding Australia's troubles leaving them on the back foot denting their momentum. Amidst the adversity, Mitchell Marsh has emerged as a beacon of hope for Australia, leading the way with a commanding presence alongside Cameron Green. Their partnership will be crucial for Australia as they endeavour to turn the tide and mount a strong comeback in the final session of the day which will come to you at 8:30 am IST (3:00 am GMT). Do stick around!

SESSION SUMMARY - 85 runs, 26 overs and 3 wickets. It was a resurgent session for the Kiwis following the lunch break, as they tightened their grip on the game with a strong comeback. Despite initial inconsistencies in their lines and lengths, the New Zealand bowlers succeeded in curbing the flow of runs from the bat. Matt Henry, in particular, provided the perfect start by swiftly dismissing Marnus Labuschagne shortly after the break, setting the tone for the Kiwi resurgence. The momentum shifted decisively in favour of New Zealand when Henry breached Usman Khawaja's defences, sending the resilient batter back to the pavilion. The dismissal of Travis Head by William O'Rourke further solidified their ascendancy, as the Kiwis asserted their authority and surged ahead in the contest. However, with a new partnership forming, Tim Southee will be eager to capitalize on any opportunity to break through and further enhance New Zealand's position in the game.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second session of Day 1! Some final words being spoken by Tim Southee in New Zealand huddle before they spread out to take their respective field positions. Usman Khawaja and Marnus Labuschagne are all set to resume their innings for Australia. Tim Southee is at the top of his mark and will kick things off with the ball in this session. Away we go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

As for New Zealand, having won a crucial toss, they would have loved to pick up a couple of wickets more, but they will take heart from the fact that they did not let Australia get away. Skipper Tim Southee had no hesitation in bowling first, wanting to make first use of the greenish-looking surface. Matt Henry set the tone by beating the bat on several occasions, while Tim Southee was as disciplined as ever. There were encouraging signs for William O'Rourke and Scott Kuggeleijn, and the inexperienced duo did well to test the Aussie openers. However, none of the four Kiwi pacers used were able to make the favourable bowling conditions count and were guilty of bowling a tad too short. It took a while, but Henry was rewarded for his patience as he got rid of Steven Smith with not much left to go for Lunch. With still movement on offer, New Zealand will be on the hunt for early wickets in the afternoon session and test Australia's middle order. Join us back at 6.10 am IST (12.40 am GMT) for the start of the second session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 62 runs, 27 overs and 1 wicket. End of an attritional session of Test cricket and it will be Australia who will be the happier of the two sides as the players walk off for Lunch! After being inserted into bat under overcast conditions, the onus was on their openers to see off that first hour safely. Steven Smith and Usman Khawaja did not let them down, as both batters applied themselves to keep the Kiwi pacers at bay. Smith was busy out in the middle and was quick to punish loose deliveries, whereas Khawaja grew in confidence as the innings progressed after a shaky start. Having put in the hard yards in the first hour or so, the Aussie openers cashed in when run-scoring got easier in the second hour. Smith could not see himself through till Lunch after which Usman Khawaja and Marnus Labuschagne joined hands to ensure there were no more casualties. Despite losing Smith, Australia have laid a good platform on which their batters will look to build in the next session.

While Australia enter the Test series with soaring confidence after their impressive T20I series win. With a recent shuffle in their batting order, Australia have opted for continuity by fielding an unchanged lineup, with the opening pair of Steven Smith and Usman Khawaja. In the bowling department, despite favourable conditions for seamers, fringe quicks like Scott Boland and Michael Neser will miss out and the frontline trio of Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, and Josh Hazlewood will continue their formidable partnership. This Australian lineup appears to be a formidable force, however, they are set to face off against a resilient New Zealand side known for their fighting spirit and tenacity. The Kiwis have won their last 5 Test matches at Wellington but haven't managed to win a Test against the Aussies since 1990. Can the Kiwis turn the tide this time around and emerge victorious against their trans-Tasman rivals? We will find out soon as the Toss and team news comes to you in a bit.

The hosts have faced formidable challenges in Test cricket against the Aussies over the past three decades, but their status as one of the strongest contenders for the World Test Championship does instil a different mindset altogether. Despite the retirement announcement of Neil Wagner and Devon Conway being ruled out due to an injury, this relatively inexperienced lineup will be determined to adopt a positive approach on the field. They will aim to capitalize on the pace-friendly conditions offered by the wicket, seeking to dismantle the Australian batting lineup which has shown vulnerability against pace in recent times.

Greetings and a warm welcome to Day 1 of the highly anticipated series opener, marking the commencement of a thrilling two-match Test series between cricketing giants New Zealand and Australia at the historic Cello Basin Reserve in Wellington. Following their impressive clean sweep in the T20I series, Australia are geared up to extend their dominance over the Kiwis in what is anticipated to be a thrilling Test series.
